He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] and was selected by the Spurs 14th overall in the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Bryant grew up in [[Riverside, California]] and initially attended [[Fountain Valley High School]], where he was coached by his father D'Cean.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/06/24/dcean-bryant-leaves-fountain-valley-to-become-basketball-coach-at-sage-hill/|title=D'Cean Bryant leaves Fountain Valley to become basketball coach at Sage Hill|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He transferred to the [[Sage Hill School]] in [[Newport Beach, California]] after his father was hired to coach at the school.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/04/05/brandon-benjamin-carter-bryant-shea-joko-win-john-r-wooden-award/|title=Brandon Benjamin, Carter Bryant, Shea Joko win John R. Wooden Award|first=Steve|last=Fryer|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} Bryant was named the [[Pacific Coast Conference (California)|Pacific Coast Conference]] MVP after averaging 22.1 points, 13.7 rebounds, four assists, 2.9 blocks, and 1.6 steals per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/story/2023-04-07/daily-pilot-boys-basketball-dream-team-carter-bryant-led-sage-hill-to-memorable-season|title=Daily Pilot Boys' Basketball Dream Team: Carter Bryant led Sage Hill to memorable season|work=[[Daily Pilot]]|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He transferred a second time to [[Centennial High School (Corona, web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/five-star-arizona-commit-carter-bryant-transferring-from-sage-hill-to-corona-centennial-hs/article_5c4e6c42-f69d-11ed-bbdd-4fa960ee03f9.html|title=Five-star In a more limited role on a talented and veteran-led Arizona team, Bryant showed consistent signs of NBA potential. Following the season, he declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Bryant, Sorber, Powell, Philon to remain in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45151088/bryant-sorber-powell-philon-remain-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 16, 2025 |date=May 14, 2025}} ==Professional career== On June 25, 2025, Bryant was selected with the 14th overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-select-dylan-harper-and-carter-bryant-in-the-first-round-of-2025-nba-draft|title=Spurs Select Dylan Harper and Carter Bryant in the First Round of 2025 NBA Draft|date=June 25, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 25, 2025}} Bryant was later included in the [[2025 NBA Summer League]] roster of the Spurs.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-announce-2025-summer-league-roster|title=Spurs Announce 2025 Summer League Roster|date=June 30, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 30, 2025}} On July 3, 2025, the Spurs announced that they signed Bryant.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2025-14th-overall-pick-carter-bryant|title=Spurs Sign 2025 14th Overall Pick Carter Bryant|date=July 3, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 3, 2025}} On January 8, 2026, Bryant received his first assignment to the [[Austin Spurs]].{{Cite tweet|author=Austin Spurs|title=Assigned & ready💪 Carter Bryant will be available for tomorrow night's matchup vs. the South Bay Lakers at 7 PM CT|number=2009340356056563985|user=austin_spurs|date=January 8, 2026|access-date=January 8, 2026}} Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] | 37 || 5 || 19.3 || .460 || .371 || .695 || 4.1 || 1.0 || 0.9 || 1.0 || 6.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Bryant is a grandchild of deaf adults. His maternal grandparents graduated from [[Gallaudet University]], the first school for the advanced education of the deaf and hard of hearing in the world. His grandfather, Mike “Doc” Torres, played for Gallaudet's basketball team and later became a member of the USA Deaf Basketball Hall of Fame. His grandmother, Shelly Freed, is a longtime educator and administrator at the [[California School for the Deaf, Riverside]]. His father, D’Cean Bryant, was a coach for the girls' basketball team at the school, after playing four seasons of college basketball at [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]]. His mother, Sabrina Torres, is a sign language interpreter.{{Cite web |title=Team Player {{!}} Arizona Alumni |url=https://alumni.arizona.edu/arizona-magazine/winter-2025/team-player |access-date=July 12, 2025 |website=alumni.arizona.edu |language=en}}{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/arizona-5-star-commit-carter-bryant-is-fueled-by-family-support-ua-connections/article_aca365a4-f1bf-11ed-9e2b-eb6a57b81719.html|title=Arizona 5-star commit Carter Bryant is fueled by family support, UA connections|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=May 13, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} Fluent in [[American Sign Language]], Bryant became an ambassador for Gallaudet University in the lead-up to the 2025 NBA draft.{{Cite web |title=Carter Bryant |url=https://gallaudet.edu/carter-bryant/ |access-date=July 12, 2025 |website=Gallaudet University |language=en-US}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{basketball stats}} *[https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/carter-bryant/16818 Arizona Wildcats bio] *[https://www.usab.com/players/carter-bryant USA Basketball bio] {{San Antonio Spurs current roster}} {{2025 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bryant, Carter}} [[Category:2005 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Arizona Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Austin Spurs players]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:San Antonio Spurs draft picks]] [[Category:San Antonio Spurs players]]
